content.text: The text argues that architecture should imitate Nature’s processes—not its forms—balancing construction, ornament, symmetry, utility, and beauty. It distinguishes classical, Gothic, pagan, and modern copying styles, advocating living, collective progress toward new architecture. Architecture also records ethnographic and historical development. Turanian peoples are portrayed as despotic, religious, artistic builders; Semites as monotheistic, literary, commercial, and architecturally restrained; Celts as warlike, artistic, and Gothic; Aryans as scientific, self-governing, practical, and less artistic. Egyptian architecture progresses from pyramid tombs and simple temples to monumental Theban palace-temples, while later Ptolemaic work declines. Assyrian architecture is primarily palatial, colorful, and archaeologically reconstructed from ruins. Daniel travelled to the office, then to the hallway; Mary moved to the office, and John went back to the hallway.
